pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Intermittent Porphyria (AIP) THE SMOKING GUN: The combination of light-induced port-wine urine and catastrophic motor paralysis triggered by CYP450-inducing anticonvulsants (phenobarbital/phenytoin) in the setting of severe caloric restriction. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Acute Intermittent Porphyria is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by a partial deficiency of porphobilinogen deaminase (PBGD) in the heme synthesis pathway. Severe fasting and CYP450 inducers (like barbiturates and phenytoin) massively upregulate hepatic ALA synthase-1 (ALAS1). Due to the downstream enzymatic block, neurotoxic heme precursors—specifically delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) and porphobilinogen (PBG)—accumulate in massive quantities. This leads to autonomic instability (hypertension, tachycardia), central nervous system dysfunction (psychosis, seizures, SIADH), and severe axonal motor neurotoxicity progressing to rapid motor paralysis. PBG spontaneously polymerizes and oxidizes upon exposure to air and light, yielding porphobilin and uroporphyrin, which turn the urine a characteristic dark port-wine color.
